title: HPC-01: HPC outlet temperature rising
text:
Compressor Section Maintenance Manual (fictional training document) | HPC-01: HPC outlet temperature rising
Signature: HPC outlet temperature (s3) sits clearly above its healthy typical level and keeps climbing, often together with HPC outlet static pressure (s11) rising.
Likely causes: fouled or eroded compressor blades, worn blade-tip clearances, leaking seals. All of these reduce compressor efficiency, so the air leaves hotter.
Actions: borescope-inspect HPC blades and tip clearances; check the date of the last compressor wash and wash if overdue; compare the efficiency trend over the last 50 cycles.
Escalate if: the rise continues across consecutive checks or fuel flow ratio (s12) starts dropping.

title: HPC-02: HPC pressure and fuel flow shifts
text:
Compressor Section Maintenance Manual (fictional training document) | HPC-02: HPC pressure and fuel flow shifts
Signature: HPC outlet static pressure (s11) drifting up while HPC outlet pressure (s7) or fuel flow ratio (s12) drifts down.
Likely causes: internal air leakage, stator vane wear, compressor stall margin loss.
Actions: leak-check the compressor casing and seals; inspect variable stator vanes for wear and correct angle; review fuel flow trend.
Escalate if: pressure and fuel flow keep diverging over the next 20 cycles.

title: LPC-01: LPC outlet temperature rising
text:
Compressor Section Maintenance Manual (fictional training document) | LPC-01: LPC outlet temperature rising
Signature: LPC outlet temperature (s2) slowly higher than its healthy typical level.
Likely causes: early-stage fouling of low-pressure compressor blades, leaking bleed valve.
Actions: inspect LPC blades for deposits; test the bleed valve for leakage; clean if fouled.
Escalate if: HPC outlet temperature (s3) is also rising; see HPC-01.

title: FAN-01: Bypass ratio increasing
text:
Fan and Bypass Manual (fictional training document) | FAN-01: Bypass ratio increasing
Signature: bypass ratio (s15) creeping above its healthy typical level.
Likely causes: core components losing efficiency so the airflow balance shifts, or eroded fan blades.
Actions: inspect fan blades for erosion or damage; check bypass-duct seals; if compressor or turbine sensors also drift, follow HPC-01 and TUR-01.
Escalate if: bypass ratio keeps rising together with core temperatures.

title: FAN-02: Fan and core speed deviation
text:
Fan and Bypass Manual (fictional training document) | FAN-02: Fan and core speed deviation
Signature: fan speed (s8), core speed (s9), corrected fan speed (s13) or corrected core speed (s14) drifting away from typical for the same load.
Likely causes: bearing wear, imbalance, control sensor drift.
Actions: check vibration and bearing condition; calibrate speed sensors; inspect shaft couplings.
Escalate if: speed deviation grows or vibration rises.

title: FAN-03: Bypass-duct pressure abnormal
text:
Fan and Bypass Manual (fictional training document) | FAN-03: Bypass-duct pressure abnormal
Signature: bypass-duct pressure (s6) away from typical.
Likely causes: duct leakage, damaged acoustic liner, loose panels.
Actions: inspect duct panels and seals for gaps; pressure-test the duct.
Escalate if: pressure keeps changing across consecutive checks.

title: POL-01: Urgency levels
text:
Maintenance Policy (fictional training document) | POL-01: Urgency levels
Level 1 WATCH: risk below the alarm line and estimated cycles left above 60. Keep routine checks and re-review at the next scheduled check.
Level 2 PLAN: risk at or above the alarm line, or estimated cycles left between 30 and 60. Schedule an inspection within the next 20 cycles and pre-order likely parts.
Level 3 URGENT: estimated cycles left between 10 and 30. Inspect at the next available stop and restrict to light duty.
Level 4 STOP: fewer than 10 cycles left, or risk above 95% with several sensors worsening. Take the machine out of service and inspect before any further use.

title: POL-02: Before any inspection
text:
Maintenance Policy (fictional training document) | POL-02: Before any inspection
Isolate power and apply lockout/tagout. Record the sensor readings and cycle count. Use only approved tools and log every finding in the maintenance record.

title: POL-03: Several sensors drifting together
text:
Maintenance Policy (fictional training document) | POL-03: Several sensors drifting together
When three or more sensors drift together, treat it as general gas-path wear rather than a single faulty part. Raise the urgency by one level and inspect the whole path, not just one component.

title: POL-04: Limits of predictions
text:
Maintenance Policy (fictional training document) | POL-04: Limits of predictions
Model risk and remaining-life figures are statistical estimates, not diagnoses. Confirm by physical inspection before replacing any part, and record the outcome so the models can be improved.

title: TUR-01: LPT outlet temperature rising
text:
Turbine and Cooling Manual (fictional training document) | TUR-01: LPT outlet temperature rising
Signature: low-pressure turbine outlet temperature (s4) above its healthy typical level.
Likely causes: turbine blade wear, loss of cooling air, or inefficient upstream compressors passing hotter air.
Actions: borescope-inspect turbine blades; check cooling flow (see COOL-01); review compressor findings (see HPC-01).
Escalate if: temperature rises while coolant bleed flow falls.

title: COOL-01: Coolant bleed flow dropping
text:
Turbine and Cooling Manual (fictional training document) | COOL-01: Coolant bleed flow dropping
Signature: HPT coolant bleed (s20) or LPT coolant bleed (s21) below typical.
Likely causes: clogged cooling passages, leaking or stuck bleed valves, worn seals. Less cooling can overheat turbine blades.
Actions: inspect and flow-test bleed valves and lines; clear blocked passages; inspect turbine blades for heat damage.
Escalate if: coolant flow keeps falling or turbine outlet temperature (s4) rises.

title: BLD-01: Bleed enthalpy rising
text:
Turbine and Cooling Manual (fictional training document) | BLD-01: Bleed enthalpy rising
Signature: bleed enthalpy (s17) above its healthy typical level.
Likely causes: compressor inefficiency heating the bleed air, heat soak in the core.
Actions: verify against compressor temperatures (see HPC-01 and LPC-01); inspect bleed lines for damage.
Escalate if: other core temperatures are also rising.
